items.headline: Hurricane Isaias nears the Gulf Coast
items.summary: Isaias became the first Atlantic hurricane of the season and strengthened to Category 2 as it approached the Gulf Coast. Residents are preparing for heavy rain, wind, storm surge and flooding this weekend.

items.headline: Russian strike on Kramatorsk bus stop kills dozens
items.summary: A Russian strike near a bus stop in Kramatorsk, in Ukraine's Donetsk region, killed dozens and halted local public transport. Power outages in Kyiv worsened.

items.headline: Houthi attacks on Saudi airports kill 3
items.summary: Houthi rebels struck several Saudi airports, killing three people and injuring 36. The attacks come as the war in Yemen intensifies.

items.headline: South Korea recalls envoy to Ukraine, tests hypersonic weapon
items.summary: South Korea will recall its ambassador to Ukraine after President Lee Jae Myung demanded an apology over a dispute about North Korean prisoners of war. Seoul also test-flew its first domestically developed hypersonic weapon after a North Korean hypersonic test.

items.headline: Army finds systemic failures behind D.C. midair collision
items.summary: A newly released Army report found failures in air traffic control, helicopter routes, training and safety practices. The Army called for safety fixes.

items.headline: Midterm map widens as GOP spending worries grow
items.summary: Republicans worry a $1 billion effort may not prevent midterm losses, while both parties pour money into about 60 competitive House districts. Kansas has emerged as an unexpected Senate battleground.

items.headline: Pike recovering after failed execution; Hasan execution to be livestreamed
items.summary: Christa Pike's attorneys say she is walking with help and eating after surviving Tennessee's execution attempt, and a judge ordered evidence preserved. The Pentagon said Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan's firing-squad execution will be livestreamed.

items.headline: ICE used New Jersey warehouse as detention site, neighbors say
items.summary: Neighbors say ICE has used a warehouse in northern New Jersey to detain migrants throughout the summer. NPR examined their claims.

items.headline: Crypto regulator shrinks as markets grow
items.summary: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission's staff and enforcement activity have fallen sharply. The agency must still write new rules for crypto and prediction markets.

items.headline: Syrian general accused of atrocities shielded in Lebanon
items.summary: A joint NPR and BBC investigation found that a former Syrian general wanted for crimes against humanity lives in Lebanon. He has funding and protection from U.S. and Lebanese officials, the investigation found.

digest.overview:
Hurricane Isaias, the first Atlantic hurricane of the season, strengthened to Category 2 as the Gulf Coast braced for landfall expected early Saturday between Mississippi and the Florida Panhandle. An Army report on the midair collision near Washington, D.C., found systemic failures in air traffic control, helicopter routes and training. Christa Pike is walking with help and eating after Tennessee's failed attempt to execute her, her attorneys said. The Pentagon said Nidal Hasan's firing-squad execution will be livestreamed. Homeland Security proposed raising work-training fees for international students to $70,000. A judge extended White House access for three news outlets. Republicans worry a $1 billion midterm push may come too late, and Kansas has emerged as a Senate battleground.

Abroad, a Russian strike near a bus stop in Kramatorsk killed at least 33 people as blackouts worsened in Kyiv. Houthi attacks on Saudi airports killed three and wounded 36. South Korea will recall its ambassador to Ukraine over a dispute about North Korean prisoners of war, and it test-flew its first homegrown hypersonic weapon after a North Korean test. Russia denied reports of a second suspected plague case linked to a Siberian lab. French high school students staged mass protests over school conditions, and Spain's housing protests deepened ahead of a Nov. 29 snap election. Israel's election, under three weeks away, is focusing on Netanyahu's handling of Oct. 7. WWF reported monitored wildlife populations have fallen 73% on average since 1970.

home.overview:
Cleveland refused to go quietly, scoring six runs in the sixth inning to beat the White Sox 9–5 and force a winner-take-all ALDS Game 5 on Saturday night in Cleveland; Patrick Bailey and José Ramírez homered. The winner opens the ALCS at Tampa Bay on Monday, while the Dodgers and Brewers start the NLCS on Sunday night in Milwaukee. In the NFL, the Buccaneers grabbed their first win, 24–16 at Dallas, behind rookie Jalon Daniels and Bucky Irving's 165 rushing yards, as the Cowboys lost CeeDee Lamb to a quad injury. Sunday opens with Eagles–Jaguars in London. In the NBA preseason, LeBron James and Joel Embiid debuted for Philadelphia in a 114–108 loss to Brooklyn.

Club soccer is back tonight, with Bundesliga leaders Dortmund hosting Werder Bremen, before Sunday's headline clash of Liverpool vs. unbeaten Man City at Anfield. Barcelona, perfect in La Liga, host Getafe and Real Madrid host Villarreal on Saturday, and the Champions League returns Oct 13–14 with Man City vs. PSG. In K League 1, Daejeon beat Jeonbuk 2–1 and Gangwon climbed to third with a 2–0 win over Bucheon, while leaders FC Seoul, 15 points clear, host Jeju SK on Saturday. In K League 2, Suwon FC and Seoul E-Land both won to close within two points of Suwon Samsung.

brief: Cleveland forced a deciding Game 5 by beating the White Sox 9–5 in Chicago, scoring six runs in the sixth inning to break a tie.
Patrick Bailey homered off the bench and drove in two, José Ramírez homered, and Travis Bazzana's RBI double put Cleveland ahead.
ALDS Game 5 is Saturday at 8 p.m. ET in Cleveland (TBS); the winner meets Tampa Bay, which swept the Yankees.
The NLCS opens Sunday at 8 p.m. ET in Milwaukee, with Game 2 Monday at 5 p.m. ET, after the Dodgers ousted Atlanta and the Brewers beat San Diego.
The ALCS starts Monday at 8 p.m. ET at Tampa Bay.
